text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3.86% today, continuing a sharp two-week slide of 17.8% from its late-October peak. The stock's recent collapse appears tied to political uncertainty following the midterm elections and mounting concerns about regulatory headwinds — Democratic control of Congress is expected to bring investigations into energy deals and policy reversals, creating near-term risk for a refiner with significant exposure to government policy and geopolitical decisions.

The broader refining picture isn't helping: while refineries are running near full capacity at 94.5%, oil prices have stayed relatively soft (US crude at $99.64), and storage levels for gasoline and diesel remain high. This combination typically squeezes refining margins, limiting the upside that would normally offset political risk for energy stocks.
